newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong paper slides on interest rate hike fears.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong paper slides on interest rate hike fears.

text.p: Hong Kong government paper tumbled in line with U.S. Treasuries on Friday as anxiety mounted over a possible interest rate hike, dealers said.

The seven-year Exchange Fund note yielded 7.87 percent by the noon close, versus 7.81 percent on Thursday, while the five-year yielded 7.50 versus 7.45 and three-year stood at 6.91 against 6.85 percent.
One-week bill yields rose to 5.00 percent from 4.98.
"U.S. jobless claims were higher than expected yesterday and players are afraid of an interest rate hike," a dealer with a European bank said.
But the dealer added that so far Hong Kong paper had suffered less than U.S. Treasuries.
Money market activity was quiet as players chose to stay sidelined until key U.S. payroll data comes out later in the day, a dealer with an American firm said.
Overnight money was markedly higher at 5-3/8 1/4 against Thursday's 5-1/8 percent while three-month cash stood at 5-11/16 5/8 percent, unchanged.
